The chapters in [*ggplot2: field manual*](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/fm-ggp2/) use a few small helpers for callout boxes and filtering. This vignette covers what each one returns and how to use it in a Quarto chunk.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(fmggp2)
```

## Callout boxes

`co_box()` and `status()` print the markdown for a [Quarto callout](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html). They return nothing; the markdown is the side effect. That means you'll need `results: asis` in the chunk options, otherwise Quarto shows the raw markdown instead of the callout.

### `co_box()`

The `color` argument picks the callout type: `"b"` (note), `"g"` (tip), `"r"` (important), `"o"` (warning), or `"y"` (caution).

```{r}
#| label: co-box-markdown
co_box(color = "b", header = "Note", contents = "Simulated data is reproducible with `set.seed()`.")
```

With `results: asis`, the same call renders as a callout:

```{r}
#| label: co-box-render
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
co_box(color = "b", header = "Note", contents = "Simulated data is reproducible with `set.seed()`.")
```

Set `fold = TRUE` to collapse the callout and `look` to `"simple"` or `"minimal"` to change its appearance.

### `status()`

`status()` marks how complete a chapter is. The `type` argument is one of `"polish"`, `"dev"`, `"draft"`, or `"complete"`.

```{r}
#| label: status
#| results: asis
status("complete")
```

## Not in

`%nin%` is the negation of `%in%`. I've found it reads more naturally than `!(x %in% y)` inside `dplyr::filter()`.

```{r}
#| label: nin
c("AOL", "Napster", "Netscape") %nin% c("Napster")
```
